criteria.semantics: Expanded from its definition: a native <ul> named by its label (aria-label), each tag a <li>, a link when it has one.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.

keyboard.key: Tab (a tag that is a link)
keyboard.outcome: Moves through the tags' links in order.

criteria.name: The tag-list's label.
criteria.role: List, with its number of tags.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the tags grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the tags wrap, none cut off, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <ul> element.
The list is named by its label in aria-label.
WHEN I reach the tags with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR the list's name and how many tags it has.
WHEN I Tab to a tag that is a link I HEAR its text and the role of link.

criteria.semantics: Expanded: a list of its tags, each after a bullet, a link when it has one. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit List of ListItems, named by its label.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the tag-list by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

keyboard.key: Tab (a tag that is a link)
keyboard.outcome: Moves through the tags' links in reading order.

criteria.name: The tag-list's label.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the tags grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the tags drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the tags at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the tags drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the tags whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A tag-list adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE a tag that is a link drawn as a link, in the accent color and underlined.
WHEN I reach the tags with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR the list's name, how many tags it has, and each tag.

announce.api: AXList, its label as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::List).
ControlType List of ListItems, its label as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_LIST, its label as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
